side_a: CC 2.4 "**membership events** (`membership:widening:v1` / `removal:v1` / `resignation:v1`, cosigned, beside the single-signer proposal, acceptance and decline)"
side_b: CC 3.1.3.2 "a widening or removal is cosigned under the group's `consensus_protocol`, a resignation is signed by the leaving member"
note: CC 2.4 lists the resignation among the cosigned events, and the roster-fold comment of `resolve_community` and `resolve_family` says "revocations, widenings, resignations, each admitted per CURRENT consensus_protocol". CC 3.1.3.2 and CC 3.3.4 make it the leaver's own single-signer row, and the family model agrees (cosign none on resignation). A door built from CC 2.4 or the fold comment holds a member in the group until a quorum signs. The rest of the document supports the leaver alone (exit is the member's own).

side_a: CC 5.3.3.1 On epoch roll the DEK changes, so a reset counter lives in a different keyspace
side_b: CC 5.3.3.1 Substrate MUST reject a chunk-append whose `(stream_id, seq)` collides with an existing sealed chunk (the replay and forking guard).
note: CC 5.3.3.2.5 sets the nonce counter equal to the header chunk_seq. Read with the first side, chunk_seq restarts at each epoch (and only a restart makes the forced roll before 2^32 avoid a wrap); read with the second side and CC 5.3.3.3 (leaves in seq order, tree_size the chunk count of the whole stream) seq is unique across the stream and never restarts. The two builds derive different nonces from epoch two on, or one refuses the other's chunk 0 as a collision. Nothing states whether chunk_seq is per epoch or per stream; CC 3.3.13 (sequence_start, HLS sequence numbers) leans per stream

side_a: CC 3.1.9.2 **reserved — substrate-steward-emitted**, the emitter rule pinned at mint per R2(a), so the ProducerSteward default never applies
side_b: manifests/family_model.json regime:{artifact}:{version} signer_rule (code-v61): who any_registered, via none; transitions.json attest roles: registered
note: The text reserves regime rows to the substrate steward; the data admits any registered key and cites no section. The cell is read from the store; the text is the only rule stated.

side_a: CC 3.4.5 `consent:state:granted` / `consent:state:revoked`, `consent:scope:*`, `consent:stream:*` MUST be emitted by a `subject_key_id` of the target Contribution or a `delegates_to` chain rooted at one

note: The text admits a delegate on a chain rooted at a subject for consent:state as for scope and stream; the data's consent:state cell has no chain and adds the owner of the node named in for_key_id, which the text does not state for this leaf.

side_a: CC 4.4.3.5.4 or under a `legal_hold` ([CC 4.4.3.2.8](#4.4.3.2.8)), the `withdraws` is admitted and recorded, and the descent it would force is refused with reason
side_b: formal/derivation/family_default_row.json erasure_route: purge (steward purge on a cosigned notice); legal_hold: none in code (162 families carry it); manifests/reactions.json and transitions.json hold no legal_hold entry
note: The text gives a legal hold a gate in front of withdrawal-driven descent and three hard_case emissions (set, lifted, violation_attempt); the data's erasure route has no hold, and no reaction emits those rows. A withdrawn record under hold is kept by the text and descends by the data.

side_a: CC 4.2.1.3: "**It is a cosigned row by a strict majority of the standing roster** (`additional_scrubs[]`"
note: The resumption and the confirmation are cosigned by a strict majority in CC 4.2.1.3, 4.2.1.1, 3.1.1 and 3.4.1, and CC 4.2.1.3 says "never a lone signature". The family model's cosign cell (read from the shipped store) says none, while its own count cell and the transition case (leaf=active: cosigned accord_majority) agree with the text. A reader of the cosign cell admits a one-holder resumption.

side_a: CC 3.1.3.1: "**Projection ceiling: `Cohort` at every commons tier, with no `authority` branch (normative — not a default).**"
side_b: data manifests/family_model.json session:{kind} placement: "any of {self_collective, targeted_family, targeted_room, commons}, signer-chosen (GAP: no per-family constraint)"
note: The text forbids a session claim above the cohort (an attendance map of a person's devices); the model cell lets the signer place it in the commons, where the replication cell serves it to everyone. The cell is marked a gap; the text has the value.

side_a: CC 3.1.3: "**Yes — addressed:** a member of the room; reach is the named tally member only"
side_b: data manifests/family_model.json census:member:share replication.audience: "cohort_plus_subjects(full) (refers-to: attested, subjects, for_key_id)"
note: Same fault as C383 on the sibling family: the text holds a member's community cell with its author and the one tally member it is addressed to; the model cell keeps the default audience (the whole cohort plus subjects) under an `addressed` placement.

side_a: CC 3.1.9.7: "its `supersedes`, `withdraws` and `recants` stand only when they too are cosigned under the same protocol"
side_b: data manifests/transitions.json goal:{scale} supersede: roles "author", policy "selfAct"
note: For a Goal a group declared, the text requires the amendment, retirement and disowning to be cosigned under the group's protocol; the model has cosign_rule none and one-signer supersede and withdraw, so one member who signed first amends or retires the group's Goal alone. The same holds for approach, method and progress_measure rows a group declares.

side_a: CC 4.3: "on window expiry it re-routes to the live quorum"
side_b: CC 4.3: "re-routes under rule 1 to the party's other live seats and, with none, to the conferrer"
note: Who answers a deferral whose Wise Authority has lapsed: rule 1 and the `deferral:request` row of CC 3.1.9.3 send it to "the live quorum", a body; the seat rule sends it to the other seats this party conferred and then to the conferrer (for an agent, its steward), and CC 4.3 says there is no roster of Wise Authorities. A reader of rule 1 alone routes an agent's deferral to a board the steward never seated. The seat rule is the later and more specific text.

side_a: CC 4.5.5: `is_named_moderator(·, C, moderate)` for the relevant community
side_b: data manifests/transitions.json: moderation:{allegation_type} attest guard "when(not moderate(signer,object)) subject(signer,ref:content_sha256) else refuse"
note: the CC 4.5.5 duty-holder table gives a moderation event to named moderators only; the guard also admits the content's subject signing it, while the same transition's roles cell says moderate with condition not_subject. Text and the roles cell agree; the guard is the odd one

side_b: data manifests/family_model.json: moderation:{allegation_type} body "moderation subject digest required (moderation_subject_digest)"
note: the signed-object table and the CDDL make `subject_sha256_ed25519_raw` optional on a moderation row and refuse only a malformed one; the family model's body cell (source prose) requires it, so a row without the digest is admitted by one and refused by the other

side_a: CC 3.4.5: **`consent:state:expired`** alone by `substrate_persist`, the one substrate-emitted consent leaf
side_b: data manifests/family_model.json: consent:state:{stance} signer_rule who ["self", "owner_of_subject(for_key_id)"], one cell for granted, revoked and expired
note: the text gives the `expired` stance to the substrate under the longest-pattern rule and the other two to the subject side; the data has one family and one signer cell, so the substrate's `expired` row fails the door and a subject may sign one

side_a: CC 4.2.1.3: The substrate MUST reject a `lifecycle:active` whose `resumes_halt_id` does not match the currently-active CONSTITUTIONAL halt
side_b: data manifests/transitions.json: accord:lifecycle:{kind} attest guard "when(leaf=confirmed) one accord:invoke:constitutional:{halt_id}@admitted[object=object] within(accord_halt) else refuse"
note: the data guards the confirmation against a named, admitted halt and states nothing for the resumption: no guard that `resumes_halt_id` names the active halt and none for a duplicate `invocation_id`. A stockpiled resumption naming another halt is refused by the text and passes the data's door

side_a: CC 5.1: "Once a member leaves, subsequent content is sealed under a key that member cannot derive."
side_b: data manifests/transitions.json membership:{stage} attest change: "resignation[scope:self|family]: key=stop_wrap"
note: The change cells rotate the epoch on `removal[scope:community|affiliations]` and stop wraps on a resignation at self or family, and have no cell for a resignation from a community or affiliation (only the ephemeral last-member case). The text rotates on any departure (5.1 'leaves'; 4.5.12.1 'rotation on departure'; CC 3.2 'Resignation and removal are one row kind at the fold'). As data, a member who resigns keeps reading.

side_b: data manifests/family_model.json consent:state:{stance} signer_rule: "self | owner_of_subject(for_key_id) x none x {}"
note: The text lets a subject's proxy on a delegates_to chain sign a consent state (CC 3.3.1 step 2, CC 4.4.3.5.5), and the card's fold cell reads `signer:subject|proxy`. The family's signer cell (code-v61) has no delegation arm, while the parent row consent:{kind} gives state `x delegates_to(chain rooted at a subject)`. Two cells of one manifest disagree on whether a proxy's grant is admitted.

side_a: CC 3.2: The age band is the I1 band (`age_self_declared` / `age_assurance:*`
side_b: CC 3.4.13: The guardian MUST be ≥ `age_assurance:provider:adult` as a floor, and the guardianship relationship to that specific child MUST be verified.
note: CC 3.2 admit_user_steward_binding takes the steward's adult band from either prefix and asks only for the steward's signature; Q3 requires a provider-rung adult and a verified relationship to that child. An admission gate built from CC 3.2 seats a self-declared adult stranger as guardian of any identity that reads as minor (which, by the fail-secure rule, is every unassured identity). CC 3.4.11 and 3.4.13 (self graduates nobody; a verified stranger is not a guardian) support Q3.

side_a: CC 3.1.3: "A signature row is never withdrawn: a member that has sent its signature cannot recall it"
side_b: data manifests/transitions.tsv: cosign:{state} withdraw admitted withdrawn author selfAct
note: cosign:{state} has one withdraw transition, role author, no guard on the leaf. The text admits a withdraws of a pending row by its proposer only and refuses one naming a signature row. A kernel executing the transition lets a member recall a sent cosignature. The attest guard is leaf-conditioned; the withdraw is not.

side_a: CC 4.2.1: "**Durable** settings are earned by **quorum, never by having been exercised**."
side_b: data manifests/transitions.tsv: mesh_config:{key} attest none admitted steward selfAct
note: mesh_config:{key} has cosign_rule none and a one-signer steward attest with no guard on TTL. The text lets one holder set only emergency relief (threshold 1, TTL at most 72 h, not renewable back to back) and gives a durable setting to the root's own quorum. The data does not separate the two, so one steward key could write a durable setting. (C379 is the text side of the same rule.)
